neighbours.label: epistemic 'may' / 'might' about the past or a guess ('we might have said', 'they may have'; output promotes ' has', ' last', ' previous')
fire: Twenty years ago, we might have called the boy shy.
There are signs that they may have sailed to the island.
Fifty years ago, doctors might have sent her home.
A few years ago, you may have needed a travel agent.
Records hint that the monks may have brewed beer there.
A decade ago, people might have laughed at the idea.
There is evidence that the tribe may have traded with Rome.
Back then, a teacher might have punished him for that.
